cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, gets a new message from the LORD. It's for Moses' brother Aaron (Exodus 4:14), Aaron's sons and all the Israelites. That's the WHOLE group chat, friend, so nobody gets to say they missed the message.
Here's the first rule, and it's about where. Say someone from the house of Israel slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat, in the camp or outside of it.

cards.question: God says the ox, lamb or goat has to be brought somewhere to be presented as an offering to the LORD. Where?

answers.text: The entrance to the Tent of Meeting
The banks of the Jordan River

cards.question: God says a man who slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat without bringing it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting has shed blood and must be cut off from his people.
God says the Israelites will now bring the LORD the sacrifices they've been offering somewhere else. Where have they been offering them?

cards.text: Now those sacrifices come to the priest at the entrance, as peace offerings. The priest splatters the blood on the LORD's altar.
Then he burns the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. Friend, the best aroma I ever made was a kitchen full of chocolate chips, and HALF the time my biggest fan was the smoke alarm.

cards.question: Then God names what has to stop. Who must the Israelites no longer offer their sacrifices to?
God says this rule about where to bring sacrifices only lasts as long as Moses leads Israel.
God says anyone who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice but doesn't bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting is cut off from his people, even a foreigner living among the Israelites.

cards.text: Now God turns to blood: if anyone eats any blood, Israelite or foreigner, God says, "I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people." Friend, I got slid into a junk drawer and cut off from my whole family once, and I would NOT recommend it.

cards.question: Then God explains why eating blood is off-limits. What reason does He give?

answers.text: The life of the flesh is in the blood
The sickness of the flesh is in the blood
The curse of the ground is in the blood

cards.question: God says He has given the Israelites the blood on the altar to make ___ for their souls.

cards.text: So God says it AGAIN: no Israelite and no foreigner living among them may eat blood. Friend, when somebody says the same thing twice in one conversation, that's the part you write on your hand.

cards.question: When a hunter brings down a wild animal or bird that may be eaten, he must drain its blood and cover it with ___.
God's rule against eating blood only covers oxen, lambs and goats.

cards.text: Then a different case: someone, native or foreigner, eats an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts. He has to wash his clothes and bathe with water, so that's laundry day AND bath night, friend, back to back.

cards.question: Once he washes his clothes and bathes, the person who ate the dead animal stays unclean until ___.
And if someone who ate an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts skips washing his clothes and bathing, what happens?

answers.text: He owes the priest a goat
He must sleep outside the camp

cards.text: That's the end of this message, friend. But trust me, the LORD's not done talking to Moses, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: Seven of the twelve choice cards (3, 5, 8, 9, 13, 15 and 18) require facts that earlier cards neither supply nor make inferable. That goes beyond the allowed few discovery questions, leaving most choices as guesses rather than reasoned picks.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The earlier cards never mention atonement or provide a way to infer that word. The baker is being asked to supply wording they have not seen rather than a meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out that the blood must be covered with dirt rather than ashes or stones. The blank tests an unrevealed detail, so answering correctly depends on luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 17 supplies the washing and bathing but gives no clue about how long uncleanness lasts. Choosing evening over morning or midnight is therefore a lucky guess, not a reasoned pick.
